gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-savate: Commanding and a bit vintage, Woodgod stands up front with lowercase that nearly matches its capitals. And Savate follows in a cleaner, modern voice, its curves open-jawed and its crossbars slightly finer than the stems.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-sono: Woodgod carries a vintage, commanding weight, with a generous opening cut into each bowl and lowercase that stretches almost to cap height. Sono follows in a plain sans, loosely spaced and easygoing over a long read.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-stack-sans-notch: Woodgod brings a vintage, commanding swagger, its lowercase climbing nearly to the capitals and every bowl cut wide open. Stack Sans Notch then reads like rod stock: sturdy, open curves, big-bodied words.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-tiktok-sans: TikTok Sans reads modern and crisp, with lowercase rising almost to cap height. Woodgod meets it with vintage, commanding display letters, each bowl channeled wide, so the heading looks weathered while the sans below stays fresh.
gen-dafont-zombie-holocaust-fs-rowan: Rowan reads friendly and literary, its curves generously open and its thin strokes about half as heavy as the thick ones. And Zombie Holocaust crowds in above with apocalyptic, stitched-together capitals that look drawn with a single nib.
gen-fredoka-gf-marcellus-sc: Marcellus SC brings dignified, literary lettering with gently modulated strokes and terminals pulled well back, a lowercase standing like cast iron capitals. Fredoka sits above it, friendly and constant in weight.
gen-fredoka-gf-ovo: Fredoka draws every line at a constant width, friendly and rounded. Ovo follows in a serif with thin strokes only slightly lighter than the thick ones, a lofty middle band, and shallow ascenders, giving the page an authoritative, classic footing.
gen-fs-kalam-dm-sans: Kalam feels inviting and cozy, its hand-drawn lines bundled tightly together. DM Sans follows in a friendly, approachable voice with wide-set terminals on the s, which stays comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-pencerio-nunito-sans: Formal, graceful, and tightly clenched. Pencerio's calligraphic hand is best large and brief, while Nunito Sans softens the page in sans-serif form, its open-mouthed curves not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-quilon-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads literary and universal, with a subtle thick-thin cadence and a prominent x-height. Quilon does its best work as the commanding editorial voice, with large open counters, while the classic serif below is made for short stretches of reading.
